correctness.rationale: TARGET route: draft claims uniform-over-compact flow convergence (Steps 1-7) but load-bearing inferences are unproved. Step 4(b) asserts D^{h,h'}_eps satisfies the same linear discrete SHE with L^p-Lipschitz bound in h, ignoring that martingale coefficients c(eta^h) depend on h via occupations (0/1) and differ by O(1), so linearity across h is false. Step 3 asserts L^2 hydrodynamic replacement uniformly over K_eps using only envelope M_K and attractiveness with no quoted uniform Boltzmann-Gibbs/second-order estimate; Step 2/5 upgrade per-h bounds to E[sup_{h}...] without entropy/chaining in h. Toy artifact uses identical noise coefficients plus deterministic drift, assuming away the h-dependent coefficient difficulty, with ratios 2-3 showing growth not contraction, so it does not verify the analytic input. Hence essential uniform equicontinuity, joint-noise uniformity, and uniform positivity are gaps, not proof.

originality.rationale: Headline uniform-over-compact graph-Hausdorff flow convergence with Parekh Sec 3.5 modulus is not recorded and not mechanically implied by prior work. Full-text inspection of the nearest prior (Parekh 2023, arXiv:2106.07727) shows Theorems 3.7/3.8 plus Remark 3.4 prove only joint convergence for finite collections (k profiles, ordered/smooth sandwich), while Sec 3.5 pp20-21 explicitly poses compact-uniform flow convergence as an open problem lacking spatial/temporal estimates except finite sets of bounded cardinality. No broader census, dual encoding, or database covers the compact-uniform claim; finite-k joint convergence does not imply uniform compact convergence.

value.rationale: The headline, if proved, would resolve the explicit open problem stated in Parekh Sec 3.5: lifting finite-dimensional basic-coupling ASEP-to-KPZ convergence to uniformity over compacts of initial data with a common noise and graph-valued path topology. Objects (weakly asymmetric ASEP, BG rescaling, Hopf-Cole KPZ map) and invariant (uniform flow convergence) were motivated before computation, the value is not known or mechanically implied, and future work on KPZ flows could need the precise fact. It is not a textbook restatement, parameter substitution, tiny gain, or unexplained enumeration.

claim_vs_prior_implication.evidence: Parekh Sec 3.5 expressly concludes BG plus finite-k methods are enough only for finite sets of bounded cardinality and that strong spatial/temporal estimates for arbitrary compacts are missing; draft supplies no uniform Boltzmann-Gibbs rate or h-Lipschitz coefficient estimate to close that gap.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Prior work does not substantively imply the headline: lifting finite-dimensional convergence to uniformity over infinite compacts needs genuinely new uniform replacement, equicontinuity-in-h, and uniform positivity estimates that are neither proved in prior work nor in the draft.
